title: HMAC: no memory cap after first Update commits
description: Trigger: HmacSetKey (key <= 128B → ctx allocated, returns 0), then HmacUpdate with 1 byte (committed, dataSz=1), then HmacUpdate with arbitrarily large chunk. Bad behavior: the cap check (line ~1053) only fires when dataSz==0. Once committed (dataSz>0), there is no upper bound on the accumulation buffer — subsequent Updates grow it without limit via XMALLOC doubling. A caller can OOM the process by sending a small first chunk then a huge second chunk. Fix: apply the cap on every Update, not just the first; if cap exceeded after commitment, return WC_HW_E instead of CRYPTOCB_UNAVAILABLE.
